# Letter of Jeremiah Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Letter of Jeremiah 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/LJR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** A copy of a letter which Jeremiah sent to those who were to be led as captives to Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to declare to them what he had been commanded by God.

**2** Because of the sins you have committed before God, you will be taken to Babylon as captives by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians.

**3** When you arrive in Babylon, you will remain there for many years, a long period — up to seven generations. After that I will bring you out from there in peace.

**4** Now in Babylon you will see gods made of silver and gold and wood, carried on shoulders, causing dread among the nations.

**5** Take care therefore that you do not become like the foreigners and be overcome with fear of those gods,

**6** when you observe the throng before and behind them, worshiping them. But say in your hearts, "It is you, O Lord, whom we must worship."

**7** For my messenger is with you, and he himself watches over your souls.

**8** Their tongue is polished by the craftsman, and they are overlaid with gold and silver — yet they are false and cannot speak.

**9** And as a young woman who is fond of adornment takes gold and fashions a crown upon the head of her god —

**10** so also the priests remove the gold from their gods and spend it on themselves, and they give some of it to the prostitutes on the rooftop.

**11** They clothe these gods of silver and gods of gold and gods of wood with garments, as one would dress a human being —

**12** though those gods cannot save themselves from rust and moth. When they have draped them with a purple robe,

**13** they wipe their faces on account of the dust of the temple, which is thick upon them.

**14** One of them is held like a magistrate wielding a scepter over the land, yet he is unable to destroy anyone who wrongs him.

**15** He has in his hand a dagger and an axe, yet he cannot deliver himself from war or robbers.

**16** From this it is evident that they are not gods; do not fear them.

**17** For just as a ceramic vessel becomes worthless to its owner when it breaks, so too are their gods. When set up in houses, their eyes are filled with dust from the feet of those who enter.

**18** And just as the gates of a court are shut against a criminal condemned to death, so the priests bolt their temple doors with locks and bars, so that they will not be plundered by robbers.

**19** Lamps are lit for them — more than for themselves — though the gods cannot see a single one of them.

**20** They are like one of the beams of the temple. It is said their hearts are consumed by creeping things from the ground; while such creatures devour them and their garments, they do not notice.

**21** Their faces are blackened from the smoke of the temple.

**22** Bats and swallows and birds land on their bodies and on their heads; cats do the same.

**23** From this you will know that they are not gods; do not fear them.

**24** The gold that covers them for beauty — unless someone wipes away the tarnish, it will not shine; and they had no awareness even when they were being cast.

**25** They were purchased at great price, yet there is no breath in them.

**26** They have no feet and are carried on shoulders, displaying their own shame before the people. And those who serve them are also put to shame.

**27** If one of them falls to the ground, it cannot rise on its own; if someone stands it up, it cannot stand on its own; and offerings are placed before them as before the dead.

**28** Their priests sell the sacrificial offerings and pocket the proceeds; likewise their wives salt away some of it; but to the poor and helpless they give nothing.

**29** Women who are unclean or menstruating handle their sacrifices. Knowing from these things that they are not gods, do not fear them.

**30** For how can they be called gods, when women set food before gods of silver, gold, and wood?

**31** And in their temples the priests sit with garments rent, with heads and beards shaved, and with heads uncovered.

**32** They wail and cry before their gods as some do at a funeral banquet.

**33** The priests strip the robes from the gods and dress their own wives and children with them.

**34** Whether harm or good is done to them, they cannot repay it. They cannot appoint a king or depose one.

**35** Likewise they cannot give riches or money; if someone makes a vow to them and does not keep it, they do not hold him to account.

**36** They cannot rescue a man from death or deliver the weak from the strong.

**37** They cannot restore sight to a blind man; they cannot rescue a man in distress.

**38** They will not show mercy to a widow; they will do no good to an orphan.

**39** Their gods of wood, stone, gold, and silver are like the stones of a mountain; those who worship them will be put to shame.

**40** How then is it fitting to suppose or say that they are gods?

**41** Even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them; for when they hear of a mute man who cannot speak, they bring Bel and ask him to articulate, as though he could perceive.

**42** And yet they themselves cannot grasp this and forsake these gods, for they have no perception.

**43** Women girded with cords sit along the highways, burning chaff.

**44** And whenever one of them is drawn aside by a passerby and lies with him, she taunts the woman next to her because that one was not judged worthy as she was, and her cord was not broken.

**45** Everything done for them is false; how then is it fitting to suppose or say that they are gods?

**46** They are manufactured by carpenters and goldsmiths; they will be nothing but what the craftsmen want to make them.

**47** And those who made them will not themselves live long; how then can the things they produced be gods?

**48** They have bequeathed only falsehood and reproach to those who come after.

**49** For when war or calamity comes upon them, the priests consult among themselves where to hide along with their gods.

**50** How then can one fail to perceive that these are not gods — beings that save neither themselves from war nor from calamity?

**51** Since they are made of wood overlaid with gold and silver, it will be known afterward that they are false. To all nations and kings it will be made plain that they are not gods but the work of human hands, with no work of God in them.

**52** Who is left in any doubt that they are not gods but works of human hands, and that no work of God is in them?

**53** They cannot raise up a king over a land or give rain to men.

**54** They cannot judge a case or deliver a land from injustice, for they have no power — they are like crows between heaven and earth.

**55** For when fire falls on the house of these wooden, silver, or golden gods, their priests flee and escape, while they themselves are burned in the middle like timbers.

**56** They cannot withstand a king or an army. How then is it possible to admit or acknowledge that they are gods?

**57** Gods of wood, stone, gold, and silver cannot defend themselves against thieves or robbers.

**58** Stronger men will strip them of gold and silver and of their garments, and walk away — and the gods will not be able to help themselves.

**59** Better, therefore, is a just king than a false god; and equally, a vessel in a house that serves its owner is better than false gods.

**60** Better also are the doors of a house that protect what is inside than false gods; likewise better is a wooden pillar in a palace.

**61** For sun and moon and stars shine brightly and are sent forth for practical ends — they are obedient.

**62** Likewise, lightning when it flashes is visible; and wind blows throughout every land.

**63** And clouds, when God commands them to travel over all the earth, carry out their commission; and fire sent from above to consume mountains and forests does what it is bidden.

**64** But none of these resembles the idols in either appearance or power.

**65** From which it follows that they are not to be thought or called gods — beings unable either to render judgment or to do good to mankind.

**66** Knowing therefore that they are not gods, do not fear them.

**67** They can neither curse kings nor bless them.

**68** They show no signs in the heavens to the nations; they do not shine like the sun, nor give light like the moon.

**69** Wild animals are better than they, for animals can flee to shelter and help themselves.

**70** Therefore in no way is it clear to us that they are gods; do not fear them.

**71** For as a scarecrow in a cucumber garden guards nothing, so are their wooden, golden, and silver gods.

**72** Similarly, their gods of gold and silver and wood are like a white-thorn bush in a garden, on which every bird perches; or like a corpse thrown out into the darkness.

**73** By the purple and linen rotting upon them you will know that they are not gods; and in the end they will themselves be consumed and become a reproach in the land.

**74** Better therefore is a just man who has no idols, for he will be far from reproach.
